title: Spring Boot: autoconfiguration, starters and per-environment profiles

videos.script: A Java program that answers HTTP needs a lot of parts. A web server. A library that writes JSON. A logger. Something that hands each request to your code. {{parts}} Wiring those by hand takes days, and every project wires them the same way. Spring Boot does that wiring for you. {{boot}} You name one starter in the pom. It brings a set of libraries, at versions somebody already tested together. {{starter}} At start-up, Boot looks at what is on the classpath and configures it. Tomcat is there, so Tomcat starts. Jackson is there, so JSON works. That is autoconfiguration. And it is not magic: you can ask for a report of every decision it made, and the reason for each one. {{report}} Then the same jar has to run on your laptop and on a server. A different port, more logging on one of them, a different database later. Profiles and external configuration do that, with no rebuild. {{profiles}} In this lesson you write the bookshop's first files by hand, and read every line of them. By the end it starts, it answers, and when two settings disagree you know which one wins. {{bookshop}}
